messages:
Rin (AE): Quick debrief from Monolith Labs POC run earlier today. Summary: sustained 180 qps baseline, two short 3-minute spikes to 450 qps. p50 ~= 35ms, p95 ~= 120ms, p99 up to ~520ms during spike ramp. Customer asked for: 1) explanation of p99 spike 2) estimate of cost delta if they want 3x burst headroom 3) note about BYOK / KMS latency. Need an ops-friendly note + cost estimate for procurement by EOD.

Diego (SRE): Artifacts posted: s3://redwood-poc/monolith/1825008888/ (requests.csv, heatmap.png, model-traces.zip). Will check replica scaling timelines and coldstart counts.

Priya (Eng): Thanks. Initial read: p99 correlated with spike start and with model shard reloading on one AZ. Also saw a short period where batch windows increased (more tokens per batch) causing tail latency for small prompt shapes. Suggestations: prewarm a small pool + staggered scale policy to avoid synchronized scale events.

Rin (AE): Load profile we ran:
```json
{"phases": [{"duration_s": 900, "qps": 180}, {"duration_s": 180, "qps": 450}, {"duration_s": 300, "qps": 180}], "avg_tokens": 280}
```

Diego (SRE): Test infra: Dedicated cluster using nvidia-gpu-a100-medium x4 across 3 AZs. Autoscaler max_replicas hit during spike in AZ-2 causing a delayed pod ready time ~14s. That aligns with p99 jump. Fix: set buffer_replicas=1 per AZ and enable staggered-provisioning flag. Also recommend KV cache prefill for top-100 prefixes.

Nina (Security): Monolith's security team asked about KMS latency and audit logs. Measured KMS calls during the test added ~8-15ms enqueue per request when using remote customer-managed keys. We can offer envelope key caching for 30s to reduce impact; document will need noted security tradeoffs (ephemeral cache window). I'll start filling vendor questionnaire items related to key management and retention.

Priya (Eng): Cost delta quick calc: for 3x burst headroom (3x 5 minutes/day) on Dedicated reserved commit: ~6-9% monthly increase (mostly idle buffer replicas). On pure on-demand: ~18-28% depending on instance family and prewarm strategy. Assumptions: same model weights, no larger kernels. Will produce table with numbers for A100 vs A10G options.

Rin (AE): Procurement wants a single number to include in renewal deck (conservative). Can we provide worst-case on-demand and a committed-discount scenario?

Priya (Eng): Yes. Worst-case on-demand (A100 family): +28% monthly. Committed 12-month reserved (same footprint + 2 buffer replicas across AZs): +7% monthly. I'll attach the spreadsheet.

artifact-bot: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-poc/monolith/1825008888/cost-estimate.xlsx

Diego (SRE): Runbook items I'll add to repo:
- set min_replicas=2 per AZ
- buffer_replicas=1 per AZ
- prewarm_hook: 120s before known surge
Example prewarm curl: 
```bash
seq 1 200 | xargs -P16 -I{} curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @small_sample.json &
```

Nina (Security): I'll include language for the customer about BYOK: expected KMS latency + envelope caching pattern and audit log export cadence. Flagging legal if they request HSM attestation.

Rin (AE): Action items: Priya to deliver cost table + conservative number, Diego to PR runbook changes, Nina to draft KMS + vendor QA answers. Need assembled one-page summary by 6pm PT for the customer.

Priya (Eng): On it 618. Will ping when spreadsheet ready.

Diego (SRE): I'll open a short internal canary checklist to validate p99 after deployment changes.

Rin (AE): Thanks y'all 44d. I'll schedule the renewal slot and send the one-pager to Monolith.
